findings.claim: Every new attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. For a consumer project targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework, none of the generated formatters or resolvers carry `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`. Yet `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in netstandard2.0 and in .NET Framework 4.0+, and is valid on classes there. So the acceptance criterion 'All generated code is decorated' is unmet for those targets with no compatibility reason. netstandard2.0 is a common target for MessagePack DTO libraries. The derived criterion allows conditional emission only when the attribute does not exist on a target. The same guard is repeated in EnumTemplate.tt, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt, UnionTemplate.tt, ResolverTemplate.tt and CompositeResolverTemplate.tt, and in their .cs counterparts.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.Req2297LegacyTargetsTests.GeneratedTypesAreDecoratedWhenConsumerTargetsLegacyFramework. It runs the generator with NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK defined in the parse options. It asserts that every generated type declaring members has an active (not #if-disabled) ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute. Expected to fail on head.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Always emit `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on every generated formatter and resolver type, with no setting and no way to opt out. This is the change's approach: the edits to the Formatter, StringKeyFormatter, Enum, Union, Resolver and CompositeResolver templates and their nested helper classes.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Emit the same attribute by default but add an opt-out setting, which the requirement calls 'fine to have too'. That needs a new boolean on the generator options (e.g. GeneratorOptions/FormattersOptions `EmitExcludeFromCodeCoverage`, default true), read from the analyzer config or MSBuild property like the other generator options. Each template would wrap the attribute lines in `<# if (Options.EmitExcludeFromCodeCoverage) { #> ... <# } #>`, with the regenerated .cs files and snapshots to match.
